title: A field with a finite speed that weighs every cost, from Ilanguage 1.b
summary: Studies, inside Ilanguage 1.b, which grip makes a field weigh every cost of a body, which fields form a long-range mark at a finite speed, whether a term on one cell of the field lets both hold in one eigenvector, whether this works with finitely many places per object, and whether the inertia of a body with its own mark follows its cost when body and field share one speed.

success_criteria.name: Which grips weigh
success_criteria.text: For a held body with a grip on a field in a stated eigenvector, near a distant held source: how the weight of the body, of its own mark and of a pair bound through the field depends on the grip function, and for which grips, field contracts and states the mark and the bond are weighed like the rest cost, for every level and both branches, and to which order.

success_criteria.name: Formation of the long-range part
success_criteria.text: After a held source is switched on: how the long-range part of the made field forms against the distance, for which field contracts and operators read by the bodies it forms at a finite speed and for which it cannot, and how that speed is related to the other speeds of the field and to the maximal speed of the bodies.

success_criteria.name: A free uniform change and an anchor
success_criteria.text: For a field of cells whose contract leaves a change applied to all cells alike free: whether the contract with held sources has a lowest eigenvector, what a term on one cell (an anchor) changes, and whether weighing, a long-range mark and its formation at a finite speed hold together in the lowest eigenvector with an anchor, and in which order of limits.

success_criteria.name: Finitely many places
success_criteria.text: Whether item 3 holds for cells with finitely many places, at every number of places or in the limit of many places, and how the grip that weighs depends on the number of places, with the smallest cells as a control.

success_criteria.name: Inertia at a common speed
success_criteria.text: In a field for which items 1-3 hold: the inertia of a moving body with its own mark against its cost, for every level and both branches, as a function of the ratio of the body's maximal speed to the speed of the field, equality included; whether weight over inertia is the same for all levels; if reached, for a bound pair.

success_criteria.name: Typical or forced
success_criteria.text: Among the grips, field contracts, field states and anchors of a stated class, how special those are that give items 1-3 and 5: typical, exceptional, or selected by a requirement stated in the terms of the language.
